To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the design of microfluidic devices for tip growing plant cell growth can be optimized to enhance trapping efficiency of pollen grains at microchannel entrances and to provide uniform fluid conditions along the growth of pollen tubes.
the flow assisted entrapments of pollen grains were successfully achieved in our PDMS biomicrofluidic platforms.
we have designed a microfluidic chip for the analysis of tip growing plant protuberances and optimized it for the entrapment of the pollen grains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a biomicrofluidic system for the study of plant cell tip growth.
developing a microfluidic device to study tip growing cells in a microenvironment, which can provide an alternative to the conventional methods for studying plant growth.
the development and optimization of a microfluidic chip for the analysis of tip growing plant cell growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed design of a PDMS microfluidic chip is suitable for the growth analysis of tip growing cells such as pollen tubes.
the microfluidic platform with 8 microchannels and 4 inlets is the most efficient in terms of uniformity of cell distribution and fluid flow conditions.

the design with the smallest inlet and outlet channels, and with a main chamber that has a width of 200 μm and a length of 500 μm, is the most efficient one to uniformly distribute the cells at the entrances of microchannels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a design with a single inlet and eight outlets is the best design to achieve uniform distribution of pollen grains at entrances of the eight microchannels.
the optimization process of the microfluidics design for the tip growth of pollen grains has been completed.
the microfluidic design was successfully tested and optimized to achieve uniform and efficient trapping of pollen grains in the microchannels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a microfluidic design can be optimized for the uniform distribution of pollen grains at entrances of microchannels and for the uniform flow conditions for pollen tube growth.
it provides an efficient method for the optimization of flow assisted entanglement of plant cells in microfluidic platforms.
the design of a microfluidic network is crucial for a successful microfluidic platform.
